subject: Custody lanes & procurement playbook for TechVista POC
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@techvista.com>, Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@techvista.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Mar 2023 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Custody lanes & procurement playbook for TechVista POC

Hi Samir / Dana —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the immediate next steps so we keep momentum into the POC: we heard three primary success criteria from your side:

- Latency under 150ms median for 1k concurrent requests (app tier)
- Model output parity on the supplied 120 eval prompts (quality)
- No production data leaves TechVista VPC during evaluation (data custody)

What I want to lock down with this thread is who owns which "custody lane" for the trial so we can finalize the tech handshake and procurement path. My recommended split (below) is based on what we discussed. Please confirm owners or propose alternates by EOD Monday.

Recommended custody lanes (high level):
- Customer networking / VPC peering & firewall rules: TechVista networking / Dana (Customer owns)
- App integration & request flow verification: TechVista app team (Samir) with Redwood SRE pairing for the smoke test
- Model serving config, batching, and KV cache controls: Redwood (Kimberly / Aditya)
- Security & audit evidence (KMS/HSM, logs, retention): Joint — TechVista security validates; Redwood provides attestations and SOC2 artifacts (Marcus leads on Redwood side)
- Procurement / SOW / billing: TechVista procurement (procurement@techvista.com) and Redwood sales ops (Laura)

Attachments: I dropped a short POC success metrics spreadsheet and a draft network diagram for the VPC peering notes. Also attached a one-page SOW draft for procurement to glance at.

Immediate next steps (what I'd like to happen now):
1) Samir: confirm app owner who will coordinate the integration pairing and list the primary contact for the smoke window (suggestion: provide 2-hour block Wed 29th).
2) Dana / networking: confirm whether TechVista will open TCP 443 between the test subnet and our connector endpoint, or if you'd prefer a private connector (we can propose an IPsec plan).
3) Procurement: loop in a point person if different from procurement@techvista.com and flag any standard terms we should preempt (data residency, indemnity, insurance).
4) Kimberly / Aditya: we will draft the execution checklist (smoke tests, perf harness, eval prompt run) and post it to the shared drive.

If you want, we can run a 30-minute internal handoff call Mon to walk the lanes and assign concrete owners.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC-success-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-network-draft.png (diagram), TechVista-SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Samir Patel <samir@techvista.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@techvista.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Mar 2023 10:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Custody lanes & procurement playbook for TechVista POC

Laura — great write up, thanks. I agree with the lane split; only tweak on the procurement side: procurement will want the SOW to call out a four-week trial with an explicit data-handling appendix. I’ll loop in our procurement lead (cc’d) to confirm.

Quick notes on owners:
- App integration lead: Me (Samir) — I’ll bring in Ben R. from our backend team for the smoke pairing.
- Networking: Dana — we can open a 2-hour window for testing on March 29 between 10–12 PT. I’ll send an invite once Dana confirms.
- Security: I’ll have our security SMB produce initial requirements; would prefer to get Redwood’s SOC2 matrix and any encryption-by-default notes (Marcus, can you confirm what you’ll share?).

On the point of data custody: we expect to keep all request/response logs within our VPC and not have them persisted on hosted Redwood storage. If a private connector is needed, please include high-level ops steps and an approximate lead time.

I can confirm Ben R. and send the availability later today. Procurement will respond by Monday.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product Engineering, TechVista
samir@techvista.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@techvista.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Mar 2023 01:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Custody lanes & procurement playbook for TechVista POC

Samir — happy to own the SOC2 artifacts and initial encryption notes. We will provide:
- SOC2 summary and control mapping (PDF)
- Encryption at rest + in transit statement and configuration checklist
- Recommended log-retention configuration for the POC (we can default to 7 days unless you prefer shorter)

On the private connector: Redwood can stand up a customer-specific connector (VPN/IPsec) — estimated lead time 5 business days from signed SOW. If you want to avoid the connector lag, we can do a scoped smoke test using mutual TLS across the public endpoint and ensure no logs are persisted in Redwood storage. Either way, we will provide an implementation runbook and a small README that Marcus (this one) will own.

I’ll put the artifacts in the shared drive and tag the checklist with owners.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@techvista.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@techvista.com>

Subject: Re: Custody lanes & procurement playbook for TechVista POC

On Mon, Mar 27, 2023 at 09:18 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

We confirm the 2-hour testing window on March 29, 10–12 PT. Ben R. will be our point for the smoke test. For the connector, procurement prefers we try the mutual TLS path first and only escalate to IPsec if we hit policy blockers. Procurement also said they will review the SOW draft and return redlines by Monday EOD.

I’ve created a short checklist item (in our internal tracker) to capture the firewall rules; I’ll share the rules in the invite.

Dana
Dana Lopez
Director, Cloud Networking, TechVista
